verdicts.reason: Quote states strap_en tells gpio to snapshot input pins; sampled_straps providing values is reasonably implied by the port set. Scenario check fits.

Quote says behaviour after the event has no effect on sampling; this is a restriction, and it is checkable every cycle from signals (sampled_straps stays stable after snapshot regardless of strap_en). Check should be both.
Only a port description ('This vector contains the sampled strap values'); no verifiable behaviour beyond what GP-T6.2-01 already covers.
Quote states the interrupt event is raised when any GPIO pin detects its configured interrupt mode.
Quote states fatal_fault alert is triggered on a fatal TL-UL bus integrity fault.

questions.question: Is the snapshot taken on the strap_en rising edge, on level high, or on a specific cycle, and how many cycles after the event do sampled_straps values become valid?
Can a later strap_en assertion (for example after reset) trigger a new snapshot, given that behaviour after the event 'has no effect'?
What are the exact interrupt modes (rising, falling, level high/low) and the latency from detection to the interrupt event?
